teile.einleitung: In a dripstone cave, cones of limestone hang from the ceiling and columns grow up from the floor. They form over a very long time from drops of water that carry dissolved limestone. In Switzerland there are several such caves, for example the Beatus Caves on Lake Thun.
wichtigste: Stalactites hang from the ceiling, and stalagmites grow upwards from the floor.
When the two grow together, a column forms, a stalagnate.
Dripstones consist of calcite, or calcium carbonate.
The limestone is deposited because the water in the cave gives off CO₂.
Dripstones usually grow only fractions of a millimetre per year.
The Hölloch in the Muotatal is over 200 kilometres long.

abschnitte.text: Rainwater seeps through the ground and takes up a lot of **carbon dioxide (CO₂)** there. This allows it to dissolve **limestone**. When this water drips into a cave, it gives off part of the CO₂ to the cave air. Now it can no longer hold as much limestone dissolved, and **calcium carbonate** is deposited. This deposit is called **calcite** or **flowstone**. Drop by drop, the dripstones grow in this way.

Dripstones that hang from the ceiling are called **stalactites**. Dripstones that grow upwards from the floor are called **stalagmites**. When the two meet, a column forms, a **stalagnate**. Very young dripstones are often thin, hollow **soda straws**. The drop runs through the inside and deposits limestone at the rim, and because of their shape they are also called macaroni. In small pools of water, round **cave pearls** can form.

Dripstones grow very **slowly**. Usually it is only fractions of a millimetre per year. How fast it goes depends on the amount of water, on the CO₂ and on the temperature. Large dripstones are therefore often many thousands of years old. Anyone who touches or breaks off a dripstone destroys in seconds what nature has created over a very long time.

Dripstones grow in **layers**, rather like tree rings. In these layers are tiny amounts of various substances, for example certain **isotopes**. Researchers can read from them how warm it used to be and how much it rained. In this way dripstones help us to understand the **climate** of past times.

Switzerland has many caves in the limestone of the Alps and the Jura. As of 2022, the **Hölloch** in the Muotatal in the canton of Schwyz is about **210 kilometres** long. It is regarded as the second-longest known cave system in Europe. The **Beatus Caves** above Lake Thun are a well-known **show cave** with dripstones. They are named after Saint Beatus.

gewusst: New passages are still being discovered in the Hölloch, so it gets “longer” with time.
In caves the temperature stays almost the same all year round, usually only a few degrees above zero in Swiss caves.

teile.einleitung: Australia is the driest inhabited continent on Earth. A large part of the country consists of deserts with red dunes, stony plains and sparse scrub.
wichtigste: Australia is regarded as the driest inhabited continent.
The dry, thinly populated interior is called the Outback.
The sand is often red because of iron oxide, that is, rust.
The Simpson Desert is known for long, parallel red dunes.
The Gibson Desert is named after an explorer who went missing.
Aboriginal people have lived in these areas for tens of thousands of years.

abschnitte.text: A large part of Australia is very dry. Australia is therefore regarded as the **driest inhabited continent**, and only Antarctica is drier. The wide, thinly populated interior is called the **Outback**. There are several big deserts there, for example the **Great Victoria Desert**, the **Great Sandy Desert**, the **Gibson Desert** and the **Simpson Desert**. Most people, by contrast, live on the coasts.

The sand in many Australian deserts is bright **red**. This comes from **iron oxide**, a kind of rust that coats the grains of sand. The **Simpson Desert** in the middle of the continent is known for its **long, parallel red dunes**. They often stretch like waves for many kilometres through the landscape. The **Great Sandy Desert** lies in the state of **Western Australia**.

In the 19th century, European explorers tried to cross the unknown interior. Many expeditions were very dangerous. The **Gibson Desert** is named after **Alfred Gibson**, a member of an expedition who went **missing** in the desert in 1874. The Simpson Desert bears the name of a sponsor who supported an expedition.

**Aboriginal people** have lived in the deserts of Australia for **tens of thousands of years**. They know water holes, edible plants and animals exactly and pass on their knowledge in stories. In the deserts today there are also **wild camels**. Their ancestors were brought to Australia by **people in the 19th century** to carry loads through the desert. Later many were set free, and they multiplied strongly.

gewusst: Australia today has one of the largest herds of wild camels in the world.
The famous red rock Uluru lies in the middle of the Outback and is sacred to Aboriginal people.

teile.einleitung: The Urubamba is a river in the Andes of Peru. It flows deep down in the valley past the famous Inca city of Machu Picchu. Its water finally reaches the Amazon.
wichtigste: The Urubamba is a river in the south of Peru.
It rises in the Andes.
Below Machu Picchu it flows through a deep gorge.
Part of its valley is called the Sacred Valley of the Incas.
Its water belongs to the Amazon river system.

abschnitte.text: The **Urubamba** rises in the highlands of the **Andes** in the south of Peru. It flows through the region of **Cusco**, the old capital of the Incas. One section of its valley is called the **Sacred Valley of the Incas**. There the Incas built terraced fields, villages and fortresses. Further downstream the Urubamba joins another river to form the **Ucayali**, which flows into the Amazon.

At **Machu Picchu** the river has dug deep into the mountains. The ruins lie high up on a mountain ridge, while the river rushes through the gorge far below. A railway line runs along the river, and many visitors travel on it to the town of **Aguas Calientes** at the foot of the mountain. The steep, wooded slopes and the river make the landscape so impressive.

gewusst: The Urubamba first flows through cool highlands and later through hot rainforest.

teile.einleitung: The Tigris is one of the great rivers of Western Asia. It rises in Turkey and flows through Iraq to the Persian Gulf. Together with the Euphrates it encloses Mesopotamia, a region where large cities arose thousands of years ago.
wichtigste: The Tigris rises in the mountains in the **east of Turkey**.
It flows through **Iraq** and joins the **Euphrates**.
The land between the two rivers is called **Mesopotamia**.
The ancient capital **Assur** lay on the Tigris.
Today **Mosul** and **Baghdad** lie on the Tigris.
In the south there are large **marshlands**.

abschnitte.text: The Tigris rises in the uplands of the south-east of **Turkey**. There it flows past the city of **Diyarbakır**, which is known for its city wall, several kilometres long, made of dark **basalt**. The wall is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. After that the river forms the border with Syria for a short stretch and then flows through **Iraq**. In the south it joins the Euphrates to form the **Shatt al-Arab**, which flows into the Persian Gulf.

The area between the Euphrates and the Tigris is called **Mesopotamia**, which means “land between the rivers”. Here some of the first cities and the earliest writing in the world arose. The city of **Assur** lay on the Tigris. It gave its name to the people of the **Assyrians** and to their chief god. Later the nearby city of Nineveh became a famous capital of the Assyrians.

In northern Iraq lies **Mosul**, one of the largest cities in the country, on the bank of the Tigris. Further south the river flows right through the capital, **Baghdad**. The water of the Tigris is very important for drinking water, fields and electricity. That is why large **dams** have been built in Turkey and Iraq. The use of the water repeatedly leads to disputes between the countries along the river.

In the south of Iraq, on the lower reaches of the Euphrates and the Tigris, lie large **marshlands**. These **Mesopotamian Marshes** are wetlands with reeds, water and many birds. The **Marsh Arabs** have lived here for thousands of years. They build houses out of reeds and travel through the channels in narrow boats. Today the marshes are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

gewusst: The Tigris is about 1,900 kilometres long. That makes it longer than the whole of the Rhine.
Baghdad lies where the Euphrates and the Tigris come especially close to each other.

teile.einleitung: A natural levee is a long, raised ridge that forms naturally along a river. It forms when the river bursts its banks in a flood and deposits sand right at the edge. The levees along the Mississippi in the USA are especially well known.
wichtigste: Natural levees are raised ridges that run parallel to the river.
They form in floods when sand is deposited at the bank.
Behind the levees lie the lower floodplains.
In English they are called “natural levees”.
On the Mississippi they are especially clear.

abschnitte.text: In a **flood**, a river bursts its banks. As soon as the water leaves the river bed, it suddenly becomes much **slower**. Slow water can no longer carry heavy grains. So it drops the coarse **sand** right at the edge. Finer material such as mud is carried further inland. After many floods a **natural levee** forms in this way, running parallel to the river.

The levees are often **higher** than the **floodplains** behind them. The floodplains are the flat, damp land beside the river. After a flood, water collects there, and swamps often form. Because the river bed also deposits material over time, a river can even flow higher than the landscape beside it. If the river breaks through its levee in a big flood, it can find itself a completely **new bed**.

On the **Mississippi** in the USA the levees are especially clear. In English they are called **“natural levees”**, that is, natural embankments. Because they lie higher and drier, people in the past liked to build houses, roads and villages there. Later they built **artificial embankments** on top of the natural levees to protect themselves better against floods.

gewusst: Many old settlements on large rivers lie on natural levees, because these often stayed dry in floods.
The soil on natural levees is sandy and well aerated, so it is good for fields.

teile.einleitung: According to the Bible, Adam and Eve are the first humans. Their story stands right at the beginning of the Bible in the Book of Genesis. It tells of the Garden of Eden, of a forbidden fruit and of why human life became hard.
wichtigste: According to the Bible, God formed Adam from earth from the ground.
The Hebrew word Adam means “human being”.
According to the Bible, Eve was made from a rib of Adam.
Adam and Eve lived in the Garden of Eden, also called Paradise.
They were not allowed to eat from the tree of knowledge.
A serpent persuaded Eve to eat the forbidden fruit.
Afterwards they had to leave the garden.

abschnitte.text: The Bible tells that God formed the human being from **earth** from the ground. Then he breathed into him the **breath of life**. The first human was called **Adam**. The Hebrew word Adam simply means “human being”. The story wants to show that humans belong to the earth and receive their life from God.

God planted a wonderful garden for the first humans. It is called the **Garden of Eden** and is often also called **Paradise**. So that Adam would not be alone, God let him fall into a deep sleep and took one of his **ribs**. From it he made the woman **Eve**. In the garden there were many trees with fruits that the humans were allowed to eat.

Only from one tree were Adam and Eve not allowed to eat: from the **tree of the knowledge** of good and evil. A cunning **serpent** spoke to Eve and claimed that the fruit was not bad at all. Eve ate some and gave some to Adam too. Incidentally, the Bible does not say that it was an apple. That was only shown that way later in pictures.

Because Adam and Eve were **disobedient**, God sent them out of the garden. From then on they had to work the field with great effort. Christians often call this story the **Fall**. It tries to explain why there is toil, suffering and guilt in life.

According to the Bible, Adam and Eve had two sons: **Cain** and **Abel**. Cain became a farmer, Abel a shepherd. Their story tells of envy and quarrels between brothers. Many people today understand the stories of Adam and Eve not as an account of real events but as a **parable** about the nature of human beings.

gewusst: That the forbidden fruit was an apple may come from the Latin word “malum”, which can mean both “apple” and “evil”.
The larynx in men is popularly called the “Adam's apple”.

teile.einleitung: An evening prayer is a prayer that you say in the evening before going to bed. Many children say it together with their parents. You think back over the day, say thank you and ask for protection during the night.
wichtigste: You say the evening prayer before going to bed.
You think back over the day that has passed.
You give thanks for good things and also think about what was not good.
Often you ask God for protection during the night, also for the family.
A well-known children's prayer begins with “Müde bin ich, geh zur Ruh”.
Many people also say the Lord's Prayer in the evening.

abschnitte.titel: A prayer at the end of the day
abschnitte.text: For many Christian families the **evening prayer** belongs to the evening. It is often said in bed, shortly before falling asleep. Some children pray together with their mother or father, others alone. You can say a well-known prayer or pray in your own words. Afterwards you usually wish each other “Good night”.

In the evening prayer you think back over the **day that has passed**. What was nice? What am I thankful for? But you also think about things that were not good, for example an argument. You can ask for **forgiveness** and end the day peacefully. Many also ask God to **protect** them in the night, themselves, their family and friends.

abschnitte.titel: Müde bin ich, geh zur Ruh
abschnitte.text: One of the best-known evening prayers for children begins with the words “Müde bin ich, geh zur Ruh, schliesse beide Äuglein zu”, which means “I am tired, I go to rest, I close both my little eyes”. It was written by the poet **Luise Hensel** about 200 years ago. The prayer rhymes and is therefore easy to learn. To this day many families in the German-speaking world know it.

Many people also say the **Lord's Prayer** in the evening. According to the Bible, the disciples asked Jesus: “Teach us to pray.” Jesus then taught them this prayer. It begins with the words “Our Father in heaven”. The Lord's Prayer is the most important prayer of all Christians and is prayed all over the world in many languages.

Instead of a prayer, some families sing an **evening song**. Very well known is “Der Mond ist aufgegangen” (“The moon has risen”) by **Matthias Claudius**. In the song, God is asked for a peaceful night. Songs and prayers in the evening help many children to become calm and fall asleep well.

gewusst: The song “Der Mond ist aufgegangen” is over 200 years old and is still often sung today.
Other religions also have fixed prayers in the evening, for example Judaism and Islam.

teile.einleitung: Do I need a jacket or an umbrella tomorrow? The weather forecast tells you. It predicts what the weather will be like in the next few days.
wichtigste: The weather forecast predicts what the weather will be.
You can find it on television, on the radio, in the newspaper and in apps.
Symbols such as sun, cloud, drops and lightning show the weather.
In Switzerland the temperature is given in degrees Celsius.
Meteorologists make the forecasts.
Weather satellites watch the clouds from space.

abschnitte.titel: Where can you find the weather forecast?
abschnitte.text: You can watch the **weather forecast** on television, hear it on the radio, read it in the newspaper or look at it in a **weather app**. It says whether it will be sunny, cloudy or rainy and how warm it will be. In this way you can prepare: pack a raincoat, take sun cream or put off the outing. Farmers, pilots and mountaineers also need the weather forecast for their work and their safety.

In the weather forecast, pictures help you understand quickly. A yellow **sun** stands for fine weather. A **cloud** means a cloudy sky, **drops** show rain and **snowflakes** snow. A **lightning bolt** stands for thunderstorms. Often you also see arrows that show where the wind is blowing from.

In Switzerland the temperature is given in **degrees Celsius**. At **0 degrees** water freezes to ice, and at 100 degrees it boils. If the temperature is below zero, we speak of frost, and the roads can become slippery. Wind speed is measured with an **anemometer**. It has small cups that turn in the wind: the faster they turn, the stronger the wind.

A **meteorologist** studies the weather and predicts it. This takes many measurements from weather stations, weather balloons and weather radars. **Weather satellites** watch the clouds from space. Big computers work out from all this data how the weather will develop. For the next few days the forecasts are quite reliable, but for two weeks ahead they become uncertain.

A **severe weather warning** means: dangerous weather is coming, for example violent thunderstorms, gales, hail or heavy rain. In Switzerland **MeteoSwiss** issues such warnings at several levels. Then it is good to stay indoors, to secure objects on the balcony and not to shelter under trees.

gewusst: Without satellites and computers, a good forecast for several days would hardly be possible.
In the past, people tried to predict the weather with country weather lore, for example from the behaviour of animals.

teile.einleitung: Wheat is a cereal and is one of the most important food plants in the world. Its grains are made into flour, bread, pasta and much more.
wichtigste: Wheat flour is used above all to bake bread.
The grains sit at the top of the stalk in the ear.
Ripe wheat glows golden yellow.
It is harvested with a combine harvester, in Switzerland mostly in July and August.
Spaghetti is made from durum wheat.
Ukraine is called the breadbasket of Europe because of its great wheat fields.

abschnitte.text: Wheat is a **grass** that is grown as a cereal. On the long stalk, the **ear** grows at the top. In it the grains sit close together. Young wheat is green, and ripe wheat glows **golden yellow**. Wheat was already grown about 10,000 years ago in the Middle East. Today it grows on all continents except Antarctica.

In Switzerland wheat is mostly harvested in **July and August**. Then the grains are ripe and dry. Today it is harvested with a **combine harvester**. It cuts off the stalks and separates the grains from the **straw**, all in one go. In the past the wheat had to be cut with a scythe and the grains threshed by hand. The straw is used, for example, as bedding in stables.

In the **mill** the grains are ground into a fine powder, which is **flour**. From wheat flour, water and yeast a dough is made, and from it **bread** is baked. Wheat contains a sticky protein called **gluten**, which makes the dough elastic. That is why it is so good for baking. Zopf, the Swiss plaited loaf, croissants and many cakes are also made with wheat flour.

There are different kinds of wheat. For bread, **soft wheat** is mostly used. **Pasta** such as spaghetti, on the other hand, is made from **durum wheat semolina**. That is why it stays nicely firm to the bite when cooked. Durum wheat likes to grow in warm, dry regions, for example in Italy.

Together with **rice** and **maize**, wheat is one of the most important cereals in the world. **Ukraine** has very fertile, dark soils. There wheat and other cereals grow in huge fields, which is why it is called the **breadbasket of Europe**. In Switzerland wheat is grown mainly on the **Central Plateau**.

gewusst: From a single grain of wheat, a plant can grow with an ear full of new grains.
The black, fertile soil of Ukraine is called chernozem.

teile.einleitung: The Dead Sea is a very salty lake between Jordan, Israel and the West Bank. Its shore is the lowest place on land on the whole Earth. In the water you can float on your back without any effort.
wichtigste: The Dead Sea is really a **salt lake**.
It is about **eight to ten times as salty** as the water of the oceans.
The shore lies **over 400 metres below sea level**.
The **River Jordan** flows in, and there is no outflow.
**Jordan** lies to the east, and Israel and the West Bank to the west.
The water level **falls** by about one metre every year.

abschnitte.text: The Dead Sea is not connected to an ocean, it is a **salt lake**. The **River Jordan** flows in from the north, and there is no outflow. In the great heat a lot of water **evaporates**, but the salt stays behind. So the water is about eight to ten times as salty as seawater. **White salt crusts** and lumps of salt form on the shore.

The water is so salty that **no fish** can live in it. Plants do not grow in the water either. Only tiny living things such as **bacteria** survive. That is how the Dead Sea got its name. At springs on the shore and in the valleys around it, however, there are certainly plants and animals.

The very salty water is **heavier** than normal water. It carries the body so well that you float on top like a cork. Many tourists have themselves photographed reading on the water. You should not get water in your eyes, though, because the salt stings badly. Some people rub themselves with the dark **mud** from the shore.

The shore of the Dead Sea lies **over 400 metres below sea level**. No other place on land lies so low. On the eastern shore lies **Jordan**, and on the other side **Israel** and the **West Bank**. High above the western shore stands the rock fortress of **Masada**. It was extended under King Herod and is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

For many years the water level of the Dead Sea has been **falling**, by about one metre every year. A lot of water is taken from the Jordan and other inflows for fields and cities. As a result, holes appear in the ground at the shore, known as **sinkholes**. How to save the lake has been discussed for a long time.

gewusst: Because of the low altitude, the air at the Dead Sea is slightly denser and contains slightly more oxygen.
In caves near the Dead Sea the famous Qumran scrolls were found, very old manuscripts.

teile.einleitung: Trinidad and Tobago is an island state in the Caribbean, not far off the coast of Venezuela. It consists of the two main islands, Trinidad and Tobago. The country is known for its carnival, for oil and for the steelpan.
wichtigste: Trinidad and Tobago lies in the southern Caribbean off Venezuela.
The capital is called Port of Spain and lies on Trinidad.
The country has been independent of Britain since 1962.
The official language is English.
Oil and natural gas are very important for the economy.
The steelpan was developed in Trinidad from old oil drums.

abschnitte.text: The state consists of the large island of **Trinidad** and the smaller island of **Tobago**, plus a few small islands. Trinidad lies only a few kilometres off the coast of **Venezuela** in South America. The capital, **Port of Spain**, is on Trinidad. Tobago is quieter and has beautiful beaches and coral reefs. The climate is warm all year round, with a rainy season and a dry season.

**Christopher Columbus** reached Trinidad in **1498**. He named the island after the Holy Trinity, “Trinidad” in Spanish. Later the islands belonged to Spain and then to **Britain**. On the plantations many people from Africa had to work as slaves, and later workers came from India. In **1962** the country became independent, and since **1976** it has been a republic.

Trinidad and Tobago has deposits of **oil** and **natural gas**. They make the country one of the wealthier states in the Caribbean. Part of the gas is liquefied and shipped to other countries. In the south of Trinidad lies the **Pitch Lake**, a natural lake of asphalt. It is regarded as the largest natural asphalt lake in the world.

The **carnival** of Trinidad is famous, with colourful costumes, parades and music such as **calypso** and **soca**. The **steelpan** was also invented here. In the 1930s and 1940s, musicians hammered old **oil drums** into shape so that they produced different notes. Today whole steel bands play with many such instruments. The steelpan is regarded as the national instrument of the country.

gewusst: The national bird is the bright red scarlet ibis, which lives in the mangrove swamps of Trinidad.
The steelpan is regarded as one of the few acoustic musical instruments invented only in the 20th century.

teile.einleitung: Wombats are sturdy, rounded animals from Australia. They dig burrows, are active at night and have a few very surprising features.
wichtigste: Wombats are marsupials from Australia.
They are rounded and have short, strong legs.
They live in burrows they dig themselves.
Wombats eat grass and roots.
Their teeth keep growing all their lives.
Their droppings are cube-shaped.

abschnitte.text: The **wombat** is one of the **marsupials**, like the kangaroo and the koala, to which it is related. The young grow up in a **pouch** on the mother's belly. In the wombat the pouch opens **to the rear**. This is practical: when the mother digs, no earth falls into the pouch. There are three kinds of wombat, and all live in Australia.

Wombats have a **rounded body with short legs** and strong claws. With them they dig long tunnels and **burrows** underground. There it is cool and sheltered. By day they rest in the burrow, and **at night** they go looking for food. If a wombat is threatened, it disappears into the tunnel and blocks the entrance with its hard rear end.

Wombats are plant-eaters. They eat mainly **grass, roots** and bark. This food is hard and wears the teeth down a great deal. That is why wombats have a special feature: their **teeth keep growing all their lives**, as in rodents. So they never become too short.

The most astonishing thing is the wombats' **droppings**: they are **cube-shaped**. Researchers found that the intestine is differently stretchy in some places and so forms the corners. Wombats like to leave their cubes on stones or tree stumps. Because they do not roll away, they serve as scent marks for other wombats.

gewusst: Wombats are the only known animal with cube-shaped droppings.
Despite their short legs, wombats can run surprisingly fast for a short time.

teile.einleitung: The term tiger economies refers to four Asian economies that developed extraordinarily fast from the 1960s onwards: South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong and Singapore. In a few decades they turned from poor areas into rich centres of industry and services. Their success is still regarded as an example of rapid development.
wichtigste: The four original tiger economies are **South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong and Singapore**.
They relied on **export-oriented industrialisation**.
**Singapore** became independent in 1965 after separating from Malaysia.
In South Korea, large family conglomerates, the **chaebol**, shape the economy.
The **Asian financial crisis** began in Thailand in 1997.
Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and the Philippines are seen as **new tiger economies**.

abschnitte.text: **South Korea, Taiwan, Hong Kong and Singapore** grew extraordinarily fast from the 1960s to the 1990s. They produced specifically for the **world market**, first simple goods such as clothes and toys, later electronics, ships and cars. Cheap labour, good schooling and **high savings rates** helped to build up industry. This strategy is called **export-oriented industrialisation**. Today all four have high incomes.

South Korea's rapid rise after the Korean War is often called the **“Miracle on the Han River”**, because the Han flows through the capital, Seoul. Large family conglomerates, the **chaebol** such as Samsung, Hyundai or LG, drove industrialisation forward with state support. **Singapore** became a state of its own on 9 August 1965 and, under Prime Minister **Lee Kuan Yew**, grew into a centre of trade and finance. In Taiwan, one of the first **export processing zones** in Asia was set up in **Kaohsiung** in 1966. There, companies could import parts free of customs duty and process them for export.

The Japanese economist **Kaname Akamatsu** described development in Asia with the **flying geese model**. Just as geese fly in a V-formation, Japan leads the way, followed by the tiger economies and then other countries of South-East Asia. Labour-intensive industries move on in turn to countries with lower wages. The more developed countries then specialise in more demanding products.

In July 1997 **Thailand** gave up the fixed link between its currency, the baht, and the dollar. The baht lost a great deal of value, and many investors withdrew their money. The **Asian financial crisis** spread to Indonesia, South Korea and other countries. Many companies went bankrupt, and people lost their jobs. Most of the countries recovered after a few years, however.

**Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and the Philippines** are often described as a second generation of tiger economies. They began their rise later and in part followed the example of the first tigers. The term “tiger” stands here for an economy that grows especially strongly and quickly. These countries too are important production locations today.

gewusst: In Japan, similar groups of companies are called keiretsu, and before the Second World War they were called zaibatsu.
Singapore is a city-state and much smaller than the canton of Zurich.

teile.einleitung: The Tokyo-Yokohama area is the largest urban area in the world. Several cities with millions of people, such as Tokyo, Yokohama and Kawasaki, have grown together here into a huge belt of settlement on Tokyo Bay. The area is shaped by ports, industry, skyscrapers and one of the densest rail networks in the world.
wichtigste: After Tokyo, **Yokohama** is the second-largest city in Japan.
Between Tokyo and Yokohama lies the city of **Kawasaki**, with over a million people.
The core of Tokyo Prefecture consists of **23 special wards**.
The **Great Kantō Earthquake** of 1923 destroyed large parts of both cities.
The **Tōkaidō Shinkansen** was the world's first high-speed line in 1964.
**Land reclamation** created a lot of new land in the bay.

abschnitte.text: Around Tokyo Bay many cities have grown together. The core of Tokyo Prefecture consists of **23 special wards**, such as Shinjuku, Shibuya or Chiyoda, each with its own administration. **Kawasaki** lies on the Tama River between Tokyo and Yokohama and is an important industrial location. **Yokohama** lies south of Tokyo and, after Tokyo, is the second-largest city in Japan. Its port was opened to foreign trade in 1859.

Since the Edo period, artificial areas have repeatedly been **filled in** in the bay. On this new land, ports, factories and residential districts were built, for example **Odaiba**. A large part of the waterfront today consists of such reclaimed land. In Yokohama, from the 1980s onwards, the business district **Minato Mirai 21** was built on old shipyard and harbour land. It was meant to strengthen Yokohama as a centre in its own right alongside Tokyo.

Every day millions of people take the train to work. At rush hour, railway staff called **oshiya** help to push passengers into crowded trains. The word means roughly “pusher”. In 1964, shortly before the Olympic Games in Tokyo, the **Tōkaidō Shinkansen** began operating. It was the first high-speed line in the world and connects Tokyo with Osaka.

Tokyo-Yokohama is the start of a long chain of cities. The **Taiheiyō Belt**, also called the Pacific Belt, stretches over about 1,200 kilometres from Ibaraki Prefecture via Nagoya and Osaka to Fukuoka. A large part of Japan's population lives in this belt. The country's most important industrial areas and ports lie here too.

On 1 September 1923 the **Great Kantō Earthquake** shook the region. More than 100,000 people died, many of them in the **fires** that followed. Large parts of Tokyo and Yokohama were destroyed. The rebuilding shaped the city planning of Tokyo. Today buildings in Japan are built to be especially earthquake-proof, and every year on 1 September disaster-protection drills are held.

gewusst: More people live in Greater Tokyo than in many European countries put together.
In Japan, 1 September is Disaster Prevention Day.

teile.einleitung: In the tropics there is a special kind of rain: zenithal rain. It falls when the sun stands almost straight overhead at midday.
wichtigste: Zenithal rain is a typical rain of the tropics.
It falls when the sun stands almost vertically at midday.
The strong sun heats the ground and the air very strongly.
The warm, damp air rises and forms tall thunderclouds.
It often rains heavily in the afternoon.

abschnitte.text: The **zenith** is the point in the sky exactly above our heads. In the **tropics**, that is, between the tropics of Cancer and Capricorn, the sun at certain times of the year stands almost **vertically** at the zenith at midday. Then it strikes the ground with full force. The air is strongly warmed and takes up a lot of moisture. **Zenithal rain** gets its name from this position of the sun.

Warm, damp air is light and rises quickly. At height it cools, and the water vapour forms huge, towering **thunderclouds**. In the **afternoon** they often discharge in heavy showers with lightning and thunder. Afterwards the sky often clears again. In many tropical regions this repeats itself almost every day in the rainy season.

Because the sun moves back and forth between the tropics in the course of the year, the zenithal rain moves with it. Areas near the **equator** have the sun at the zenith twice a year and therefore often **two rainy seasons**. Further from the equator there is usually only one rainy season and a long dry season. The zone of rising, rain-bearing air is also called the **Intertropical Convergence Zone**.

gewusst: In Switzerland the sun is never at the zenith, not even on the longest day in June.

teile.einleitung: A world language is a language that is spoken in many countries and by a great many people. Some languages have especially many native speakers, others are learned mainly as a foreign language.
wichtigste: Mandarin Chinese has the most native speakers in the world.
English is spoken by the most people overall, counting those who speak it as a foreign language.
Spanish has the second most native speakers.
The UN has six official languages, and German is not one of them.
Many official languages in Africa date from colonial times.
Swahili is an important common language of communication in East Africa.

abschnitte.text: **Mandarin Chinese** is spoken by over 900 million people as their mother tongue, more than any other language. In second place comes **Spanish**, with about 480 million native speakers in Spain and most countries of Latin America. If you count mother tongue and foreign language together, **English** is in front. About 1.5 billion people speak it, most of them as a second or foreign language. English is the most important language for science and international exchange.

The **UN** has six official languages: **Arabic**, **Chinese**, **English**, **French**, **Russian** and **Spanish**. Important documents are published and speeches are translated in these languages. **German** is not one of them. In Switzerland, incidentally, there are four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh.

In many countries the language of a former **colonial power** is still the official language. **Senegal** was a French colony, so French is the official language there. Kenya, Ghana and Nigeria were British colonies and have English as their official language. **Angola** and **Mozambique** were colonies of Portugal until 1975, and there **Portuguese** is spoken officially. Besides that, many local languages are spoken in these countries.

**Canada** has two official languages: English and **French**, which is spoken mainly in the province of Quebec. In **India**, **Hindi** is an official language of the central government alongside English. It is written in the Devanagari script. In **Indonesia**, **Indonesian** became the common official language after independence, and there are also hundreds of regional languages. In East Africa **Swahili** is widespread and is an official language in Tanzania and Kenya.

gewusst: There are about 7,000 languages in the world, and many of them are spoken by only a few thousand people.
India has hundreds of languages, which is why many different scripts appear on its banknotes.

teile.einleitung: Wind shear means that the wind changes greatly over a short distance, in its strength or direction. It is important for aviation and for the formation of cyclones.
wichtigste: In wind shear, wind strength or direction changes over a short distance.
Vertical wind shear means that at height the wind blows differently from down below.
Strong wind shear can be dangerous for aircraft when taking off and landing.
Strong vertical wind shear often prevents a tropical storm from becoming a hurricane.

abschnitte.text: The wind does not blow the same everywhere. If it changes clearly over a short distance in **strength or direction**, we speak of **wind shear**. If the difference between the lower and upper layers of air is great, it is called **vertical wind shear**. It occurs, for example, in thunderstorms, at weather fronts or behind mountains.

Wind shear can be dangerous for aircraft, especially shortly before landing or at take-off. If a headwind suddenly turns into a tailwind, the aircraft loses lift. That is why many airports and modern aircraft have **warning systems** that detect wind shear. Pilots practise in the simulator how to react correctly.

A **hurricane** needs warm sea water and a calm, even flow of air at height. If the **vertical wind shear is strong**, the storm is pulled out of shape and cannot build up well. Often a tropical storm then does not become a hurricane at all. Weather services therefore watch wind shear closely in order to predict cyclones.

gewusst: A cyclone has to build up vertically like a spinning top, and strong wind shear throws it off balance.

teile.einleitung: In many Swiss holiday resorts, flats stand empty for most of the year. With the Second Homes Initiative, the people decided in 2012 to limit the building of such flats strongly.
wichtigste: A second home is not lived in permanently, often only on holiday.
The Second Homes Initiative was launched by Franz Weber.
The people and the cantons accepted it in 2012.
The Second Homes Act has applied since 1 January 2016.
Where over 20 per cent of homes are second homes, a commune may in principle not approve any new ones.
The Lex Koller regulates the purchase of property by people abroad.

abschnitte.text: A **second home** is a flat in which nobody lives permanently. Often it belongs to people who use it only on holiday, for example for skiing in winter. In holiday resorts people then speak of **“cold beds”**: the flats **stand empty for most of the year**, and the shutters are closed. This is difficult for village life, because shops and restaurants have fewer customers and housing for locals becomes scarce and expensive.

The environmentalist **Franz Weber** launched the federal popular initiative “Stop the unlimited building of second homes!”. On 11 March **2012** the people and the cantons narrowly accepted it. Since then the Federal Constitution has said that the share of second homes in a commune may be at most **20 per cent**. Supporters wanted to protect the landscape, while opponents feared disadvantages for the building trade and for tourism in the mountain regions.

To put the initiative into effect, Parliament passed the **Second Homes Act**. It has been in force **since 1 January 2016**. If a commune's share is above 20 per cent, it may **in principle not approve any new second homes**. There are exceptions, however, for example for managed holiday flats that are regularly let to guests.

A commune has **1,500 homes**, of which **400 are second homes**. You calculate 400 divided by 1,500, which gives about **27 per cent**. That is more than 20 per cent. The commune therefore may in principle **not approve any new second homes**. In many mountain cantons such as Graubünden and Valais, numerous communes lie above this limit.

Another law is the **Lex Koller**. It regulates the **purchase of property by people abroad**. Anyone who does not live in Switzerland may buy houses or flats here only with permission and under restrictions. The law is named after the former Federal Councillor **Arnold Koller**.

gewusst: The Second Homes Initiative was accepted very narrowly, with about 50.6 per cent yes votes.
In some holiday communes, more than half of all homes are second homes.

teile.einleitung: In the desert it is scorching hot by day, but at night it can turn surprisingly cold. This desert climate has to do with the sky and the ground.
wichtigste: Deserts are very dry, and it hardly rains.
By day it is hottest in the early afternoon.
At night it is often cold, because no clouds hold back the heat.
Sand stores heat badly and cools quickly.
On winter nights there can be ground frost in the Sahara.
Long, loose clothes protect against the sun.

abschnitte.text: In a **desert** it rains very little, and the sky is mostly cloudless. The sun therefore beats down on the ground unhindered. It is hottest not at midday but in the **early afternoon**. By then the ground has been heating up for hours. In the **Sahara**, temperatures of over 40 degrees in the shade can occur in summer.

After sunset it quickly turns cool in the desert. This is because there are **no clouds**. Clouds act like a blanket that keeps the heat near the ground. Without them the heat radiates unhindered into space. In addition, **sand stores heat badly** and so cools quickly. So in the Sahara it is often **cold** at night, and on winter nights there is sometimes even **ground frost**.

If the air cools strongly at night, it can hold less moisture. In the **early morning**, **dew** then sometimes settles on stones and plants. For many desert animals and plants this dew is an important source of water. Some beetles even collect the droplets on their backs.

Many desert dwellers wear **long, loose clothes** and cloths around the head. This sounds odd in the heat, but it is clever: the clothing serves **as protection from the sun** and from sand. Under the loose cloth the air can circulate. On the cold night the same clothes keep you warm.

gewusst: In some deserts the difference between day and night can be more than 30 degrees.
Only part of the Sahara consists of sand dunes, and large areas are stone and rubble desert.

teile.einleitung: Vietnam is a country in South-East Asia. It is long and narrow and has the shape of an S on the map. It is known for rice fields, Ha Long Bay and the noodle soup pho.
wichtigste: Vietnam is long and narrow like an S.
The capital, Hanoi, lies on the Red River.
The largest city is called Ho Chi Minh City, formerly Saigon.
In the south the Mekong flows into the sea.
Rice is often grown in wet fields.
After Brazil, Vietnam is the second largest coffee producer in the world.
The Vietnamese language is written with Latin letters and many accents.

abschnitte.titel: A country in the shape of an S
abschnitte.text: Vietnam lies in **South-East Asia** on the coast of the South China Sea. The country is **long and narrow** and looks like an **S** on the map. In the north lies the capital, **Hanoi**, on the **Red River**. In the south the **Mekong** flows into the sea in a large delta. There too lies the largest city, **Ho Chi Minh City**, which used to be called **Saigon**.

Many farmers grow **rice** in wet fields, the paddy fields. The deltas of the Mekong and the Red River are especially fertile. In the mountains there are also rice terraces on steep slopes. After Brazil, Vietnam is also the **second largest coffee producer** in the world. Tea, pepper and fruit are also grown.

**Ha Long Bay** in the north is famous. There thousands of limestone rocks and small islands rise out of the sea. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In central Vietnam lies the old town of **Hoi An**, with old merchants' houses and colourful lanterns. In the past, trading ships from many countries docked here.

The Vietnamese language is written today with **Latin letters**, with many accents added to show the pitch. A typical dish is **pho**, a noodle soup with herbs. In the 20th century Vietnam went through long wars. Since 1976 the country has been reunited.

gewusst: In Vietnamese the same word can mean quite different things depending on the pitch.
In Vietnam very many people get around on motor scooters.

teile.einleitung: Evaporation is the process in which liquid water turns into invisible water vapour without boiling. It happens every day everywhere: on puddles, on wet washing and on the sea. Without evaporation there would be no clouds and no rain.
wichtigste: In evaporation, liquid water turns into water vapour.
The water does not have to boil for this.
Warmth, wind and a large surface speed up evaporation.
Evaporation cools, which is why we sweat.
Evaporation is an important part of the water cycle.

abschnitte.text: Water consists of tiny particles that are constantly moving. At the surface, some particles have enough energy to escape into the air. They then become **water vapour**, which you cannot see. This also happens far below 100 degrees, which is why it is called **evaporation** and not boiling. A puddle disappears completely by itself after a while in this way.

Water evaporates faster when it is **warm**. **Wind** also helps, because it carries away the damp air above the water. A **large surface** is also important: washing spread out dries faster than a crumpled heap. If the air is already very humid, on the other hand, only a little evaporates. That is why washing dries badly on a muggy day.

To evaporate, water needs **heat**, which it takes from its surroundings. This is called **evaporative cooling**. When we sweat, the sweat evaporates on the skin and cools us down. That is also why you feel cold when you come out of the swimming pool wet and the wind is blowing. Plants also give off water through their leaves and so cool their surroundings.

Most evaporation takes place over the **oceans**. The water vapour rises, cools at height and forms **clouds**. From them rain or snow falls, which flows back into the sea through streams and rivers. This **water cycle** also supplies the lakes and glaciers of Switzerland with water.

gewusst: When sea water evaporates, the salt is left behind, which is why rain is not salty.
A large tree can evaporate several hundred litres of water on a hot summer day.

teile.einleitung: The tropics are a broad belt around the middle of the Earth. It is warm there all year round, because the sun stands very high in the sky at midday. Rainforests grow in the tropics, and fruits such as bananas, cocoa and coffee.
wichtigste: The tropics lie around the equator.
It is warm there all year round.
Day and night are almost always about 12 hours long.
Rainforest grows in the humid tropics.
Bananas, cocoa and coffee grow in the tropics.
The toucan lives in the rainforest of South America.

abschnitte.text: The **tropics** lie as a broad belt around the middle of the Earth. The **equator** runs right through them, the imaginary line that divides the Earth into a northern and a southern half. To the north and south the tropics are bounded by the **tropics of Cancer and Capricorn**. Between them the sun stands exactly overhead at midday at least once a year. That is why this part of the Earth gets especially much warmth from the sun.

In the tropics it is **warm all year round**. There is no cold winter with snow in the lowlands. The days are also always about the same length: day and night each last about **12 hours**. Often the difference between day and night is greater than the difference between the months. Instead of summer and winter, many places have a **rainy season** and a **dry season**.

Where it rains a lot in the tropics, **tropical rainforest** grows. A great many different animals and plants live there. In the rainforest of South America, for example, lives the **toucan** with its huge, colourful beak. Where there is a long dry season, **savanna** grows, a grassland with scattered trees. In Africa, elephants, giraffes and zebras live there.

Many fruits and plants need a lot of warmth and rain. That is why **bananas**, pineapples and mangoes grow in the tropics and not outdoors here. The **cocoa tree** also grows there, and chocolate is made from its beans. Switzerland buys its cocoa beans from tropical countries. **Coffee** also comes from shrubs in warm countries, for example from **Brazil**.

gewusst: There is snow in the tropics too: on very high mountains such as Kilimanjaro in Africa.
The word “tropics” comes from Greek and has to do with the “turning” of the sun at the tropics of Cancer and Capricorn.

teile.einleitung: The tropics are two imaginary lines on Earth, north and south of the equator. Over them the sun stands exactly overhead at midday once a year, and then it “turns” and moves back.
wichtigste: The northern tropic is called the Tropic of Cancer, the southern the Tropic of Capricorn.
Around 21 June the sun stands overhead at midday above the Tropic of Cancer.
The area between the tropics is called the Tropics.
The Tropic of Capricorn runs right through Australia.
The Tropic of Cancer runs through Mexico, the Sahara and India, among other places.
In Switzerland the sun is never directly overhead.

abschnitte.text: The tropics lie at about **23.4 degrees** north and south latitude. Their position depends on the **tilt of the Earth's axis**. The northern one is called the **Tropic of Cancer**, the southern the **Tropic of Capricorn**. Between them lie the **Tropics**. There the sun stands at least once a year at midday at the **zenith**, that is, exactly overhead.

At the **summer solstice** around 21 June, the northern hemisphere is tilted most strongly towards the sun. Then the sun stands overhead at midday above the Tropic of Cancer. After that, the point where it is directly overhead moves back towards the equator. Around 21 December it is overhead above the Tropic of Capricorn. The tropics get their name from this turning back.

The **Tropic of Cancer** runs through **Mexico**, the **Sahara**, **India** and **southern China**, among other places. Brazil and Peru lie south of it, Spain north of it. The **Tropic of Capricorn** runs right through **Australia**, near the town of Alice Springs. Kenya and Indonesia lie closer to the equator, New Zealand further south.

About 2,000 years ago, at the two solstices the sun stood in the zodiac constellations **Cancer** and **Capricorn**. The tropics were named after them. Because the Earth's axis moves slowly, this is no longer exactly true today. The position of the tropics changes too: the tilt of the Earth's axis is at present getting smaller, so each year they move about **15 m** closer to the equator.

Switzerland lies at about 46 to 48 degrees north, and so far north of the tropic. That is why the sun is **never** directly overhead here. Even on the longest day in June it stands at an angle in the sky at midday. That is why in Switzerland you always cast a shadow, even at midday.

gewusst: In the tropics there are days when you cast almost no shadow at midday.
At several places crossed by the Tropic of Cancer, monuments mark the line.

teile.einleitung: A thermal spring is a spring from which warm or hot water comes out of the ground. The water was heated deep in the Earth by the Earth's own heat. The Romans already liked to bathe in water like this, and Switzerland also has well-known thermal baths.
wichtigste: At a **thermal spring**, warm water comes out of the Earth.
The word “thermal” means warm.
The Romans already bathed in **Baden** in Aargau.
**Leukerbad** in Valais is famous for its thermal water.
In Japan, a bath in a hot spring is called an **onsen**.
In **Pamukkale** in Turkey, limescale forms white terraces.

abschnitte.titel: Where the warm water comes from
abschnitte.text: Rainwater seeps into the ground and flows deep down through cracks and gaps in the rock. The deeper it goes, the warmer it gets, because it is hot inside the Earth. This is called **geothermal heat**. In some places the warm water rises back to the surface. On its way it often dissolves **minerals** from the rock, which is why thermal water sometimes tastes and smells special.

The Romans already bathed in **Baden** in the canton of Aargau, and they called the place **Aquae Helveticae**. The springs are still used today. **Leukerbad** in Valais is famous for its thermal water, and many people bathe there in warm pools with a view of the mountains. The warm spring of **Bad Ragaz** rises in the **Tamina Gorge**. From there the water is piped to the village.

abschnitte.titel: Onsen and snow monkeys in Japan
abschnitte.text: Japan has a great many hot springs, because there are many volcanoes there. A bath in a hot spring is called an **onsen**. For many people in Japan, a visit to an onsen is part of everyday life and of holidays. Especially well known are the **Japanese macaques**, also called snow monkeys. In the cold winter they warm themselves in hot springs.

In **Pamukkale** in Turkey, warm water containing lime flows over a slope. When the water cools, the **limescale** is deposited. Over a long time this created white pools and terraces that look like snow. The name Pamukkale means “cotton castle”. The terraces are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

gewusst: In many parts of their empire, the Romans built baths at warm springs.
Iceland even uses hot water from the ground to heat houses.

teile.einleitung: The deep sea is the dark, cold part of the ocean below a few hundred metres. It is the largest habitat on Earth and is still little explored. Astonishing animals live there that cope with darkness, cold and high pressure.
wichtigste: Sunlight reaches only **a few hundred metres** down into the sea.
The water is usually only **a few degrees above zero**.
The weight of the water creates very high **pressure**.
Many animals produce light themselves, which is called **bioluminescence**.
**Marine snow** drifts slowly down and serves as food.
At **black smokers**, hot water streams out of the ground.

abschnitte.text: Sunlight penetrates only a few hundred metres into the sea, and below that it is **pitch dark**. The sun warms only the water at the top, and in the deep sea it is almost everywhere only **a few degrees** warm. There is a great deal of water above the deep sea. Its weight presses with great force on everything, which is called **water pressure**. People can only go down so deep in special submersibles.

Many deep-sea animals can produce light themselves. This is called **bioluminescence**. With the light they lure prey, scare off enemies or find one another in the dark. The **anglerfish** has a kind of fishing rod on its head with a glowing lure. When a fish comes closer, it snaps shut in a flash.

No plants grow in the deep sea, because there is no light. Many animals live on **marine snow**. These are tiny remains of dead animals and plants that slowly sink downwards. They look like snowflakes. Sometimes a dead whale also sinks to the bottom and feeds many living things there for years.

The **giant squid** is a squid with long tentacles. With them it can grow to about 10 metres long, and it has huge eyes. The **sperm whale** dives more than 1,000 metres deep to hunt squid. The giant squid has been filmed alive only very rarely. Much of what we know about it comes from animals washed up on beaches.

abschnitte.titel: Hot springs on the sea floor
abschnitte.text: In some places hot, mineral-rich water streams out of the sea floor. Because it forms dark clouds, these springs are called **black smokers**. Special animals live here, such as **tube worms**. They get their food not from sunlight but from bacteria that use substances from the hot water.

gewusst: The deepest known point in the oceans lies in the Mariana Trench, about 11 kilometres below sea level.
Giant squid have eyes as big as a plate, among the largest in the animal kingdom.

teile.einleitung: When the weather suddenly changes, a weather front is often involved. A front is the boundary between a warm and a cold air mass.
wichtigste: A weather front is the boundary between warm and cold air.
In a warm front, warm air slides over cold air.
A cold front often brings showers, thunderstorms and cooling.
When a cold front overtakes a warm front, it is called an occlusion.
On weather maps, fronts are drawn with special symbols.

abschnitte.text: Air is not the same everywhere: there are warm and cold, damp and dry **air masses**. When two different air masses meet, they do not mix straight away. A boundary forms between them, the **weather front**. Fronts often belong to a **low-pressure system** and move over the land with the wind. In Central Europe they mostly come from the west.

In a **warm front**, warm air slowly slides up over the colder air. Many clouds form, and it often rains for a long time and evenly. In a **cold front**, cold air pushes like a wedge under the warm air and lifts it quickly. This often brings **showers, thunderstorms** and strong wind. After it has passed, it becomes noticeably cooler, and the sky often clears.

Cold fronts are usually faster than warm fronts. When a cold front catches up with the warm front ahead of it, it is called an **occlusion**. The warm air is pushed upwards away from the ground. On **weather maps**, cold fronts are drawn with triangles and warm fronts with semicircles. An occlusion gets both symbols alternately.

gewusst: When a cold front passes, experts can often measure a marked drop in temperature within a short time.

teile.einleitung: A tropical cyclone is a huge, spinning storm that forms over warm tropical seas. Depending on the region of the sea, it is called a hurricane, a typhoon or a cyclone. It brings extremely strong wind, a lot of rain and dangerous storm surges.
wichtigste: In the Atlantic the storms are called hurricanes, in the north-west Pacific typhoons, and in the Indian Ocean cyclones.
They form only over seawater of about 26 °C and more.
In the calm centre, the eye, it is often almost windless.
In the northern hemisphere they spin anticlockwise.
From a wind speed of about 119 km/h, a storm counts as a hurricane.
Over land they weaken quickly.

abschnitte.text: Tropical cyclones have different names depending on the region. In the Atlantic and the north-east Pacific they are called **hurricanes**. In the **north-west Pacific**, for example off Japan or the Philippines, they are called **typhoons**. In the **Indian Ocean** and the South Pacific they are called **cyclones**. The same kind of storm is always meant. A tropical cyclone counts as a hurricane when the wind reaches at least force 12 on the **Beaufort scale**, which is about **119 km/h**.

Tropical cyclones form only over **warm seas**. The water has to be about **26 °C**, and that down to a depth of several dozen metres. Warm water evaporates, and the moist air rises and forms huge thunderclouds. In the process a great deal of energy is released, which drives the storm. When the storm moves over **land**, it lacks this supply of warm, moist air, and friction with the ground slows the winds. That is why it usually weakens quickly there.

At the centre of a tropical cyclone lies the **eye**. There it is often almost windless, and the sky can even be clear. Around the eye lies the **eyewall**. There the strongest wind rages, with the heaviest rain. When the eye passes over a place, the storm seems to be over for a short time. But then comes the other side of the eyewall, with wind from the opposite direction.

The **rotation of the Earth** deflects air currents, which is called the **Coriolis force**. That is why the air does not flow straight to the centre but circles around it. In the **northern hemisphere** the storms spin **anticlockwise**, and in the southern hemisphere clockwise. Right at the equator the Coriolis force is very weak. That is why hardly any tropical cyclones form there.

Besides the wind, **heavy rain** and **storm surges** are especially dangerous. The storm pushes the seawater against the coast, and low-lying areas are flooded. In **2005** **Hurricane Katrina** brought a storm surge that broke flood defences in **New Orleans** in the USA. Large parts of the city were under water. Today weather services watch the storms with satellites and warn people in good time.

gewusst: A large tropical cyclone can have a diameter of several hundred kilometres.
The storms are given names from lists that the World Meteorological Organization draws up in advance.

teile.einleitung: A transform fault is a boundary between two tectonic plates where the plates slide sideways past each other. No new crust is created, and none is lost. Boundaries like this are known for strong earthquakes, for example in California or in Turkey.
wichtigste: At a transform fault two plates **slide sideways past each other**.
Crust is **neither formed nor destroyed**, which is why such boundaries are called **conservative**.
The term was introduced by **John Tuzo Wilson** in 1965.
The best known is the **San Andreas Fault** in California.
**Strong earthquakes** are typical, and volcanoes are usually absent.
The **North Anatolian Fault** and the **Dead Sea Transform** are also examples.

abschnitte.text: The Earth's surface consists of large **plates** that move slowly. At some boundaries they move away from each other, and at others they collide. At a **transform fault** they slide **sideways** past each other. In the process, Earth's crust is neither newly formed nor destroyed. That is why such boundaries are also called **conservative plate boundaries**, meaning boundaries that preserve.

The Canadian geophysicist **John Tuzo Wilson** introduced the term in 1965. He recognised that faults between the sections of a **mid-ocean ridge** are a kind of plate boundary in their own right. These ridges are broken into many segments that are offset sideways by transform faults. Only the piece between the ridge ends is active. The extensions are called **fracture zones**. The **Wilson cycle** is also named after Wilson.

The **San Andreas Fault** in California separates the **Pacific Plate** from the **North American Plate**. It is one of the best-known transform faults on land. **Los Angeles** lies to the west of it on the Pacific Plate, which is slowly moving north-west towards San Francisco. In **1906** the fault ruptured along several hundred kilometres. The earthquake and the fires that followed destroyed large parts of **San Francisco**.

The plates do not move smoothly. They **catch** on each other, strain builds up and is then released with a jolt. This creates shallow, often **strong earthquakes**. There are usually no volcanoes at transform faults, because no molten rock forms there. Geologists watch such faults closely in order to judge the danger better.

The **North Anatolian Fault** runs across the north of Turkey and separates the Anatolian Plate from the Eurasian Plate. Along this fault there have repeatedly been severe earthquakes, for example in 1999 near **Izmit**. The **Dead Sea Transform** runs through the Jordan Valley and the Dead Sea. Here the Arabian Plate slides northwards past the African Plate. The Dead Sea lies in a basin along this fault.

gewusst: At the San Andreas Fault the Pacific Plate moves only a few centimetres a year, about as fast as fingernails grow.
In many millions of years, this could make Los Angeles lie next to San Francisco.

teile.einleitung: The tiger is the largest cat in the world. It lives in Asia, from the hot forests of India to the cold east of Russia. With its striped coat it is one of the best-known and most beautiful animals of all.
wichtigste: The tiger is the **largest species of cat**.
Its coat is **orange with black stripes**.
Every tiger has its **own stripe pattern**.
More than half of all wild tigers live in **India**.
Tigers are **loners** and good swimmers.
They mostly hunt at **dusk and at night**.

abschnitte.text: The tiger is the largest species of cat, even a little bigger and heavier than the **lion**. Its coat is **orange with black stripes**. In tall grass and in the forest this makes it well camouflaged, because the stripes look like shadows. No tiger has the same stripes as another. Researchers can therefore recognise individual tigers by their **stripe pattern**.

Tigers live only in **Asia**. More than half of all wild tigers live in **India**, where there are many protected areas. The **Bengal tiger**, also called the royal Bengal tiger, lives mainly in India and neighbouring countries such as Bangladesh and Nepal. The **Siberian tiger**, or Amur tiger, lives in the cold east of Russia. Its thick coat protects it from snow and cold.

Adult tigers mostly live **alone**. Each tiger has its own **territory**, which it marks with scent marks and scratch marks. Unlike many other cats, tigers like **water**. They are good swimmers and like to lie in the cool water on hot days. Young tigers stay with their mother for about two years and learn hunting from her.

Tigers mostly hunt at **dusk** and at night. They creep up quietly and surprise their prey from a short distance. Their food includes deer, wild boar and other large animals. Many hunts fail, so a tiger often has to try several times before it is full.

In the past there were many more tigers than there are today. They lost large parts of their habitat, and many were hunted. Today the tiger is **seriously endangered** and strictly protected. In India and other countries, numbers have grown again thanks to protected areas. Zoos too, such as Zurich Zoo, take part in programmes to preserve tigers.

gewusst: A tiger's skin is also striped under the fur.
The roar of a tiger can be heard for kilometres.

teile.einleitung: Toucans are colourful birds from the forests of Central and South America. Their most striking feature is their huge, brightly coloured beak. It looks heavy but is surprisingly light, and it even helps the bird to cool down.
wichtigste: Toucans have a huge, colourful beak.
They live in the forests of Central and South America.
The beak is airy on the inside and therefore light.
Toucans eat mainly fruit.
They can give off excess heat through the beak.

abschnitte.titel: A bird with a big beak
abschnitte.text: The most striking thing about the **toucan** is its huge, colourful **beak**. In some species it is almost as long as the body. Depending on the species, it glows yellow, orange, red, green or black. There are about 40 different species of toucans. The largest is the **toco toucan**, with a bright orange beak.

Toucans live in the **forests of Central and South America**, many of them in the tropical rainforest. They do not occur in Africa or Asia. They usually stay high up in the **treetops**. There they often fly from tree to tree in small groups. They build their nests in **tree holes**, where they lay their eggs.

The big beak is surprisingly **light**. Inside it is built like a **sponge**, with many small air chambers. On the outside it has a thin covering of horn. A lot of **blood** flows through the beak. If the toucan gets too hot, it can **give off heat** through its beak, rather as an elephant does through its big ears.

Toucans eat mainly **fruit**. With their long beaks they can also reach fruit on thin twigs that would not bear their weight. They often toss the fruit briefly into the air and catch it again with the beak. Now and then they also eat insects, small animals or the eggs of other birds. Because they pass seeds out again in their droppings, they help to spread plants in the forest.

gewusst: To sleep, the toucan turns its head and lays its beak on its back.
The beak of the toco toucan can grow to about 20 centimetres long.

teile.einleitung: Uti possidetis is a principle of international law. It says that new states take over the borders that existed when they became independent. It became especially important when colonies in Africa and Latin America became independent.
wichtigste: Uti possidetis comes from Latin and means roughly “as you possess”.
New states take over the borders of the former colonies.
The Organisation of African Unity committed to it in Cairo in 1964.
In this way wars over borders were meant to be avoided.
South Sudan came into being in 2011 as a rare exception.
In 2002 the International Court of Justice awarded the Bakassi Peninsula to Cameroon.

abschnitte.text: **Uti possidetis** is Latin and means roughly “as you possess”. In **international law** this means that a new state keeps the borders that applied when it became independent. These were often the former administrative borders of a **colony**. The principle was already applied in the 19th century in **Latin America**, when the Spanish colonies became independent. It is meant to prevent disputes over who owns which territory.

Many borders in Africa were drawn by colonial powers, often with no regard for peoples and languages. Even so, in 1964 in **Cairo** the **Organisation of African Unity** decided to respect the existing borders. People feared that otherwise disputes over new borders would break out everywhere. That is why the borders of Africa have rarely changed since. One of the few exceptions is **South Sudan**, which separated from Sudan in 2011.

When states cannot agree about a border, the **International Court of Justice** in The Hague can decide. It then often examines where the border ran in colonial times. A well-known example is the **Bakassi Peninsula**, over which Nigeria and Cameroon quarrelled. In 2002 the court awarded it to **Cameroon**. Nigeria handed over the territory a few years later.

gewusst: The expression originally comes from old Roman law, where it was about the possession of plots of land.

teile.einleitung: Tiwanaku is an ancient ruined city in Bolivia, not far from Lake Titicaca. Long before the Inca Empire it was an important centre in the Andes. The best-known feature is the Gate of the Sun, made from a single block of stone.
wichtigste: Tiwanaku lies in **Bolivia**, south of **Lake Titicaca**.
The city is **older than the Inca Empire**.
It lies at a height of about **3,800 metres**.
The **Gate of the Sun**, made from a single block of stone, is famous.
Tiwanaku is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

abschnitte.text: Tiwanaku was the centre of a culture that flourished in the Andes long **before the Incas**. Its heyday was roughly in the first millennium AD. From here it influenced a large area in present-day Bolivia, Peru and Chile. Later the city lost importance, though exactly why is not entirely certain. The Incas found the ruins already abandoned and regarded them as a special place.

The best-known structure is the **Gate of the Sun**. It is carved from a single large **block of stone**. At the top it is decorated with a figure and many smaller figures whose meaning researchers are still studying today. Nearby there are large **platforms**, walls of precisely worked stones and stone figures.

Tiwanaku lies about **3,800 metres** above sea level on the high plateau of the Andes, the **Altiplano**. It is cool there, and the air is thin. The people nevertheless grew enough food, for example potatoes. To do so they laid out raised fields with water ditches. Since 2000 Tiwanaku has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

gewusst: The Gate of the Sun weighs several tonnes and was carved from a single stone.

teile.einleitung: Where is the wind blowing from? Wind direction answers this question. It is important for the weather, for sailors and for aircraft.
wichtigste: Wind direction says where the wind comes from.
A west wind comes from the west and blows towards the east.
A weather vane and a weathercock show the wind direction.
In Switzerland a west wind often blows, and the bise comes from the north-east.
Wind direction is given in compass points or in degrees.

abschnitte.titel: Named after where it comes from
abschnitte.text: For **wind direction** there is an important rule: you always name the direction **from which** the wind comes. A **west wind** therefore comes from the west and blows towards the east. A north wind comes from the north. This is different from a train, where you say where it is going. Experts also give the direction in **degrees**: north is 0 degrees, east 90 degrees, south 180 degrees and west 270 degrees.

A **weather vane** or a **weathercock** turns so that its point faces into the wind. At airfields a red and white **windsock** hangs, which fills with the wind. You can also see from clouds, smoke or flags where the wind is blowing from. Pilots take off and land into the wind where possible.

In Switzerland the wind often comes from the **west** or south-west. Such west winds often bring damp air from the Atlantic and so rain. The **bise**, on the other hand, comes from the **north-east**. It is cold and dry and often brings high fog or clear, cool weather. The **foehn** in the Alpine valleys mostly blows from the south.

gewusst: Because the wind on the Central Plateau often comes from the west, many thunderstorms cross Switzerland from west to east.

teile.einleitung: Lake Chad is a large, very shallow lake in Central Africa on the southern edge of the Sahara. It borders four countries, and millions of people live off its water. Since the 1960s it has shrunk greatly.
wichtigste: Lake Chad borders four countries: Chad, Niger, Nigeria and Cameroon.
It is only a few metres deep.
The Chari River brings it most of its water.
The lake has no outflow to the sea.
Since the 1960s it has shrunk greatly.
The country of Chad is named after the lake.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Chad** lies in the **Sahel**, the transition zone between the Sahara and the savannas further south. It borders **four countries**: Chad, Niger, Nigeria and Cameroon. The country of **Chad** bears the name of the lake, lies on its eastern shore and is the largest of the neighbouring countries in area. Not far south of the lake, on the Chari, lies the capital of Chad, **N’Djamena**.

Lake Chad is **very shallow**, only a few metres deep. For comparison: Lake Constance is over 250 metres deep at its deepest point. Most of the water is brought by the **Chari River** from the south, together with its tributary the **Logone**. The lake lies in a **drainage basin with no outlet**. Its water does not flow to the sea but evaporates or seeps away. Because it is so shallow, its area changes greatly depending on the rain.

Since the **1960s** the lake has lost a large part of its open water surface. The reasons are **droughts** and the taking of water for **irrigating** fields. It is often said that it has shrunk by about 90 per cent. This figure is, however, **disputed**, because the water surface changes greatly from year to year and a lot of the area has turned into swamp. A few thousand years ago the lake was still many times larger.

Millions of people live off Lake Chad. They **fish**, irrigate their fields and water their cattle. A special breed of cattle lives at the lake, the **Kuri cattle**. They have thick, swollen yet light **horns**, which are said to help them when swimming. Kuri cattle are adapted to life in swamps and between the islands.

gewusst: Although Lake Chad has no outflow, its water is mostly fresh, because some of it drains away underground.
There are many islands in Lake Chad, some of which are made of floating plants.

teile.einleitung: Between today's weather and the climate over decades there is something in between: the weather pattern, or spell of weather. It describes how the weather runs its course over several days to weeks.
wichtigste: A weather pattern is the general course of the weather over several days to weeks.
Weather, on the other hand, describes a short moment.
Climate covers a period of many years.
A long heatwave or a wet week are examples of a weather pattern.

abschnitte.text: Experts distinguish three periods of time. The **weather** is the state of the air now or today. The **weather pattern** describes the typical course over **several days to weeks**, sometimes over a whole season. The **climate** sums up the weather over many years, usually over 30 years. A weather pattern therefore lies in time between weather and climate.

If it is hot and dry on almost every day for two weeks, we speak of a **summery spell** or a heatwave. A series of cool, rainy days is also a weather pattern. For agriculture the weather pattern is very important: it decides when you can sow and harvest. That is why the German word also comes from the everyday life of farmers and gardeners.

We speak of **weatherproof** materials when they withstand rain, sun and frost for a long time, for example with garden furniture. At outdoor sports events it is sometimes said that a match will take place “in all weathers”. What is meant is: even if it rains or is cold.

gewusst: Many old country weather sayings try to predict the weather pattern for the coming weeks.

teile.einleitung: The tropical wet and dry climate is found in the tropics between the permanently wet areas at the equator and the deserts at the tropics of Cancer and Capricorn. It is hot all year round, but the rainy season and the dry season alternate. The savanna is typical of this climate.
wichtigste: In the tropical wet and dry climate, the rainy season and the dry season alternate with high temperatures all year round.
In the Köppen-Geiger system it corresponds mainly to the savanna climate Aw.
The rainy season comes with the moving Intertropical Convergence Zone.
Near the equator there are often two rainy seasons, and towards the tropics only one.
The typical vegetation is the savanna.
Brasília is an example of this climate.

abschnitte.text: In the **tropical wet and dry climate**, temperatures stay high all year round. The seasons are determined not by warmth and cold but by **precipitation**. A **rainy season** is followed by a **dry season**. In the **Köppen-Geiger** climate classification this corresponds mainly to type **Aw**. The w stands for “winter-dry”: the dry season falls in the time when the sun is lower.

The rainy season is linked to the **Intertropical Convergence Zone**. This is a zone in which warm, moist air rises and forms powerful thunderstorms. In the course of the year it moves north and south with the **overhead position of the sun**. Where it lies at the time, heavy **zenithal rains** fall. These usually begin **a few weeks after** the sun's highest point, because ground and air need time to warm up. When the zone lies in the other hemisphere, the **trade winds** bring dry air.

Near the **equator** the sun is at its zenith twice a year. There it can therefore have **two rainy seasons**.
